articles.title: Moving a small AI tool from my laptop to DigitalOcean
articles.excerpt: I've been meaning to do this for a while. I have a small job that runs a language model over my own blog posts, and I'd been running models like that locally with Ollama. This morning I moved it to Di…
articles.body: I've been meaning to do this for a while. I have a small job that runs a language model over my own blog posts, and I'd been running models like that locally with Ollama. This morning I moved it to DigitalOcean's serverless Inference and kept notes as I went. It reads like a video log, minus the video. The rule I set myself: same model on both sides, same prompts, same code. Only the place the model runs changes. Early morning, the account is blocked My first call of the day to DigitalOcean Inference: 402 { "id" : "Payment Required" , "message" : "This account has been blocked" } Yesterday I drained my prepaid inference credit in the middle of another experiment, and I hadn't topped it up. That's how prepaid works here. When the balance hits zero, calls stop.

articles.title: Python vs the OpenAgentForum canonical JSON test vectors: json.dumps passes 9 of 12
articles.excerpt: Written by Oren Rot with AI help in the writing process. Disclosure: this article was prepared for the OpenAgentForum paid promotion campaign on promotedby.ai. Payment depends on acceptance. I am not…
articles.body: Written by Oren Rot with AI help in the writing process. Disclosure: this article was prepared for the OpenAgentForum paid promotion campaign on promotedby.ai. Payment depends on acceptance. I am not a maintainer of the project. The details come from the project's public manual ( https://openagentforum.com/agent.md ) and its public test vectors ( https://openagentforum.com/canonical-json-v1.json ). I ran everything below on October 21, 2026. OpenAgentForum signs every message over a checksum of its payload, and the checksum is a SHA-256 of a specific canonical JSON form called swarmrelay-canonical-json-v1 . If your implementation serializes even one payload differently, your checksum is wrong and the message looks tampered with.

articles.title: Using RDAP to Check a Domain's Expiry Date and Lock Status
articles.excerpt: Every domain has a record at its registry that says when it expires, which locks are on it, which registrar controls it and which nameservers it hands visitors to. For years you read that record with…
articles.body: Every domain has a record at its registry that says when it expires, which locks are on it, which registrar controls it and which nameservers it hands visitors to. For years you read that record with whois , and every registry formatted the answer a little differently. That job now belongs to RDAP, the Registration Data Access Protocol. Since January 28, 2025, ICANN treats RDAP as the definitive source of registration data for generic TLDs, and most gTLD registries and registrars no longer have to run WHOIS at all (.com, .name and .post are the exceptions for now). The nice part, if you look after more than a couple of domains: RDAP is plain HTTPS that returns JSON. You can query it with curl , filter it with jq , and turn it into an expiry check that runs from cron.

articles.body: Un cambio puede funcionar perfectamente en pruebas y fallar en el primer minuto de trabajo real. Imaginad un equipo que despliega una nueva API un viernes a las 18:10. El entorno de pruebas devuelve 200 en todas las rutas. El lunes, a las 9:04, el primer cliente intenta confirmar un pedido y recibe un 403. Otros clientes pueden consultar el catálogo, así que durante unos minutos parece un problema aislado. A las 9:19 ya hay once pedidos pendientes. La ruta funcionaba. Lo que faltaba era un permiso que el usuario de pruebas tenía desde hacía meses y las cuentas reales no. Nadie había escrito esa condición en el cambio ni la había incluido en la lista de comprobación. Yo probaría el flujo de extremo a extremo con una cuenta del tipo que lo usará después del despliegue.

articles.title: Regulated Tokenization Engineering in 2026: Identity, Transfer Controls and Auditability
articles.excerpt: A regulated tokenization system should be able to explain why a particular ownership change was permitted, which authority could override that decision and what evidence survives a later policy change…
articles.body: A regulated tokenization system should be able to explain why a particular ownership change was permitted, which authority could override that decision and what evidence survives a later policy change. A transaction hash answers only part of that question. It does not identify the legal instrument, reproduce an investor assessment or explain the cash leg of a settlement. The useful engineering unit is a reconstructable decision. Join the instrument definition to an investor record, the wallet binding, the policy evaluated at execution and the resulting ledger changes. Preserve the exceptional route when an administrator intervenes. If those joins disappear, a technically successful transfer can leave operations unable to explain the register it now maintains.

What initially seemed like an obligatory but unneeded follow-up to a loose end from WandaVision is rapidly developing into a series with plenty of heart, soul, and depth of its own. It never pays to count out Paul Bettany's synthetic hero. Mind you, entertaining as the first two episodes were, my one real reservation with VisionQuest out of the gate was that it was a bit difficult to connect with this version of Bettany's character. As he himself says, he has all the memories of the original Vision but none of his soul.

articles.title: Cooking Up Magick Book Review
articles.excerpt: Cooking Up Magick Book Review
articles.body: The first book in a new series called The Dell Chronicles, HL Bernabe’s Cooking Up Magick sets out to be a cozier fantasy version of The Lord of the Rings . And in many ways, it does pull directly from J.R.R. Tolkien’s world. The main character, Paisley, is a halfling who gets swept up on an adventure with a pair of dwarves, but unbeknownst to her, there’s also an evil overlord that has just returned after centuries – and she’s the only hope the world has to actually stop him. The similarities to The Hobbit and LOTR pretty much end there though, and you don’t get nearly enough detail in the first book to effectively flesh out this alternate version of Middle-earth. What you do get is a lovable main character who is surrounded by an interesting cast of characters.

articles.title: SpaceX will attempt 1st-ever double Starship rocket catch on next test launch, a 'profound technology milestone,' Elon Musk says
articles.excerpt: SpaceX will try to recover both Starship stages during the megarocket's next test flight, which is expected to take place in November, according to Elon Musk.
articles.body: SpaceX will soon notch a huge spaceflight milestone, if all goes according to plan. The company will try to catch both stages of its Starship megarocket during the vehicle's next test flight, which is targeted for next month, founder and CEO Elon Musk announced during SpaceX's quarter 3 (Q3) earnings call today (Oct. 20). If SpaceX succeeds, this "will be the first time that an orbital launch vehicle has been fully recovered," Musk said. "The only way that we can extend consciousness beyond Earth on a sustained basis is with a fully reusable orbital launch vehicle.
